origins.section: A Subproblem Solved by Any Method Can Still Return a Cut
A Relaxation of the Subproblem in the Master Saves Iterations
One CP-SAT Model of the Whole Problem Checks the Answer

recorded.prompt:q-nogood: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-nogood: cap.model.add_linear_constraint(sum(cap.x[pid, y] for pid in ids) <= len(ids) - 1, name=f"nogood_{y}_{cuts}") — with core = chosen when no smaller conflict is searched, |S| - 1 = 3
recorded.prompt:q-relaxation: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-relaxation: "Weeks per season: the jobs that must happen inside a season cannot need more weeks than the season has, sum p_j x_{j,y} <= b - a". "The season rows remove the loop altogether ... every conflict is a pair of jobs that overflow their season, which is exactly what the season row states."
recorded.prompt:q-check: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-check: If the one model ever found a schedulable plan worth more than the loop's answer, the loop would be the one in the wrong, because its master is a relaxation that only a wrong cut or row can make refuse a schedulable plan.

recorded.prompt:q-nogood: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.

recorded.prompt:q-nogood:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-nogood:a: \sum_{j \in S} x_{j,y} \;\le\; |S| - 1 \qquad \text{(nogood}_{y,k}) — for four jobs the right-hand side is 3, not 2
recorded.prompt:q-nogood:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-nogood:b: "at least one of these projects starts in another year, or not at all" — the row is <= |S| - 1 = 3, not <= 0
recorded.prompt:q-nogood:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-nogood:d: sum(cap.x[pid, y] for pid in ids) <= len(ids) - 1 — the row is an upper limit, not a >= 1 row
recorded.prompt:q-relaxation:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-relaxation:a: "The 52-week row changes nothing: no year's chosen jobs come near 52 weeks; the clashes are inside seasons."
recorded.prompt:q-relaxation:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-relaxation:b: "A job allowed the whole year is not counted in a season's row, since it may run outside the season." The page counts only jobs "inside" the season, so a row over every job touching it could cut off schedulable plans.
recorded.prompt:q-relaxation:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-relaxation:c: The season row's limit is the season length, "<= last - first". A 52-week limit is as weak as the year row, and "The 52-week row changes nothing ... the clashes are inside seasons."
